title: Review: Respiratory substrates and RQ; respirometers; Plant transport: phloem and translocation; Water uptake and xerophytes; Adaptations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EX11#t4 term and clue written for the game; RS05#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV09#t2 term and clue written for the game; EV09#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV09#N.3, EX11#N.8, EX12#N.9, RS05#N.10, EV09#N.18, EX11#N.12a, EX12#N.2, RS05#N.9, EX11#N.5, EX12#N.15a, RS05#N.7. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Sink
items.clue: Place where sugars leave the phloem to be used or stored, such as a root, meristem or fruit.

items.label: Respirometer
items.clue: Sealed-tube apparatus in which a liquid bead in a capillary shows how much O₂ organisms use.

items.label: Natural selection
items.clue: Individuals with a useful allele survive and breed more, so it becomes more common over generations

items.label: Adaptation
items.clue: An inherited feature that raises an organism's chance of surviving and reproducing in its environment

options.text: A rattlesnake's venom is an anatomical adaptation, because it is delivered through the fangs.
Zebras living in herds is not an adaptation, because behaviour is not inherited.
A kangaroo rat producing very concentrated urine is a physiological adaptation.
A dog moved to a cold country growing a thicker coat during its life is an anatomical adaptation.

questions.explanation: It is a body process, carried out by the kidneys, that saves water in the desert.

questions.stem: In spring, sugars stored in the roots of a deciduous tree are converted to sucrose and carried in the phloem to the opening buds. Which statement about this transport is correct?

options.text: Mitochondria in the companion cells provide the ATP that physically drives the sap along the sieve tubes up to the buds.
Companion cells in the root use ATP to load sucrose into the sieve tubes, and the sap flows up to the buds, the sinks.
Sap cannot move upwards in the phloem, so the sugars must instead be carried up to the buds in the xylem.
The sieve tube elements must first be killed and emptied, as in xylem, before any sap is able to flow through them.

questions.stem: A cut stem of a well-watered plant exudes sap from the xylem for several hours. When the roots are treated with a respiratory inhibitor, the exudation stops. What does this show about how the sap was being pushed out?

options.text: Root cells were actively transporting water into the xylem, and this active transport of water molecules needs ATP from respiration.
The exudation was caused by tension pulling water up the xylem, and the inhibitor stopped the transpiration that generates it.
The xylem vessels themselves were using ATP from respiration to push the sap upwards, and the inhibitor stopped them.
Root cells were using ATP to pump mineral ions into the xylem, so water entered by osmosis and produced a positive pressure.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. A student measured oxygen uptake by yeast (cm³ g⁻¹ min⁻¹) at five temperatures: 20 °C 0.10; 30 °C 0.19; 40 °C 0.31; 50 °C 0.26; 60 °C 0.04. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Rate rises with temperature over the whole range, so the low reading at 60 °C must be an experimental error.
Rate rises with temperature up to an optimum near 40 °C, then falls as the enzymes of respiration denature.
Above 40 °C the yeast switches to anaerobic respiration, which uses no oxygen, so oxygen uptake falls.
At 60 °C the extra carbon dioxide produced expands and pushes the liquid back, hiding the true rate.

questions.stem: Arctic foxes have much smaller ears than fennec foxes. Which statement best explains how small ears became typical of Arctic foxes?

options.text: Each Arctic fox's ears shrank during its life in the cold, and its cubs inherited the smaller ears.
Foxes with alleles for smaller ears lost less heat, so survived and bred more; the alleles spread.
The cold caused new mutations for small ears to arise in the foxes that needed them.
Small ears are better in every environment, so in time all foxes will evolve them.

questions.stem: A young leaf near a shoot tip is still expanding. It imports sucrose through the phloem. Weeks later, fully grown, the same leaf exports sucrose. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Now it makes more sugar than it uses, so its companion cells load sucrose: it has become a source.
When young, the leaf received its sugar in the xylem, because phloem only ever carries sap out of leaves.
As the leaf aged, its sieve tubes died and became lignified, which reversed the direction of flow.
Mitochondria in the leaf's companion cells switched from pushing sap in to pushing sap out.

questions.stem: In a transverse section of a dicotyledonous root, where are the xylem and the phloem found?

options.text: In separate vascular bundles arranged in a ring near the outside of the root, in just the same way as in the stem.
At the centre of the root, with the xylem forming a star shape and groups of phloem between its arms.
At the centre of the root, with phloem forming a star shape and xylem in groups between its arms.
Spread throughout the cortex, which conducts water and sugars across the width of the root.

questions.explanation: The dicotyledonous root has a central vascular cylinder: xylem forms a star or cross shape in the middle and phloem lies in separate groups between the arms of the xylem. This is surrounded by the cortex and then the epidermis bearing root hairs.

questions.stem: Yeast in a respirometer was studied for 10 minutes. With potassium hydroxide present, the bead moved towards the yeast by a volume of 45 mm³. Without potassium hydroxide, the bead moved away from the yeast by 9 mm³. What is the RQ?
questions.explanation: O₂ used = 45. Moving away means CO₂ released = 45 + 9 = 54. RQ = 54 ÷ 45 = 1.2. Above 1: some anaerobic respiration.

questions.stem: Which feature of a sieve tube element helps sap to flow along the phloem?

options.text: It is dead and empty like a xylem vessel, so there is nothing inside the cell to slow the flow of sap.
Its end walls are solid plates that hold the sap under pressure so that it flows faster along the tube.
It contains many mitochondria, whose ATP is used to push the sap along the tube towards the sink.
It has lost its nucleus and most of its cytoplasm and organelles, so little inside it obstructs the sap.

questions.stem: A gardener scatters a large amount of fertiliser on dry soil around a plant. Within a day the plant wilts, although the soil has not dried further. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Root hair cells take in water whenever the plant needs it, so the wilting must have started in the leaves.
The fertiliser ions poisoned the pumps that actively transport water molecules into the root hairs.
The ions lowered the soil's water potential below the root hair cells', so water stopped entering by osmosis.
The ions raised the soil water's potential, so water drained away from the roots faster than it could be absorbed.

questions.stem: In a respirometer, carbon dioxide is absorbed by potassium hydroxide. With 5.0 g of germinating seeds, the gas volume in the apparatus fell by 1.2 cm³ in 10 minutes. What is the rate of respiration per gram?

options.text: 0.024 cm³ of carbon dioxide produced per gram per minute
0.12 cm³ of oxygen taken up per gram per minute
0.024 cm³ of oxygen given out per gram per minute
0.024 cm³ of oxygen taken up per gram per minute

questions.explanation: The fall in volume equals the oxygen consumed, as the alkali removes carbon dioxide. 1.2 ÷ 10 ÷ 5.0 = 0.024 cm³ g⁻¹ min⁻¹.
